result: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals were born at Mendelian ratios but died neonatally of severe anemia. Deletion of Lsd1 during embryonic development was incomplete in fetal liver but complete in newborn bone marrow. Blood counts and bone marrow cellularity were significantly reduced, and the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell compartment was vastly distorted with >30-fold reduction in LS+K+ and LS-K+ cells.
evaluation: Claims C24-C34 are well-supported by Western blot data (C26, C27), blood count data (C28), cellularity measurements (C29, C30), and flow cytometry analysis (C31-C34) shown in Figure 1. The data consistently demonstrate severe hematopoietic defects in VavCre-mediated Lsd1 deletion.

result: Poly(I:C) injection in Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice resulted in efficient Lsd1 inactivation, massive reduction in peripheral blood counts, and death within 7-10 days. Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre animals were largely deficient in LS+K+ and LS-K+ cells. The frequency of lin- CD150+ CD48- Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells increased fourfold with twice as many cells proliferating, and these cells clustered with wild-type LT-HSCs in single cell qPCR analysis.
evaluation: Claims C35-C42 are supported by Western blot and PCR data (C35), blood count data (C36), survival data (C37), flow cytometry (C38, C39), cell cycle analysis (C40, C41), and single cell qPCR clustering (C42) shown in Figure 2 and supplementary figures. The data demonstrate efficient Lsd1 deletion and severe hematopoietic defects in the Mx1Cre system.

result: In methylcellulose colony assays, control LT-HSCs generated large CFU-GEMM colonies, whereas Lsd1-deficient colonies were smaller and consisted almost exclusively of immature blasts. Lsd1 knockout colonies primarily consisted of lineage-negative c-Kit+ Sca-1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells, while wild-type colonies were largely composed of mature Gr1+ Mac1+ myeloid cells. These data indicate that Lsd1 function is vital for efficient differentiation of LT-HSCs into more mature myeloid progenitor cells.
evaluation: Claims C43-C47 are supported by colony assay morphology data (C43, C44) and flow cytometry analysis of colony composition (C45, C46) shown in Figure 2D-J. The conclusion (C47) is appropriately inferred from multiple converging lines of evidence including flow cytometry, qPCR, and colony assays.

result: In competitive bone marrow transplantation experiments, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells showed severely reduced contribution to myeloid lineages (barely detectable at 4 weeks), progressive decline in B and T lymphoid lineages (>50% decrease at 4 weeks), and only 2-14% of mature cells in spleen and 1-9% in bone marrow at 12 weeks. At 12 weeks, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells contributing to HSCs and various progenitor populations were virtually undetectable. These data implicate Lsd1 as a crucial epigenetic guardian of HSC self-renewal and homeostasis.
evaluation: Claims C48-C53 are supported by comprehensive transplantation data shown in Figure 3B-F, demonstrating progressive loss of Lsd1-deficient cells across all hematopoietic lineages and stem/progenitor compartments. The conclusion (C53) is appropriately inferred from the transplantation data showing competitive disadvantage and loss of Lsd1-deficient HSCs.

result: Mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes were almost absent from the bone marrow of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice, with concomitant accumulation of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. Loss of Lsd1 culminates in a differentiation block at the transition of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ to mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes.
evaluation: Claims C54-C56 are supported by flow cytometry data (C54) shown in Figure 4A,B and cytospin preparations. The inference of a differentiation block (C56) is appropriately drawn from the accumulation of immature cells and loss of mature granulocytes. However, the manuscript does not provide direct evidence ruling out alternative explanations such as selective survival of immature cells.

result: EpoRCre-mediated deletion of Lsd1 was lethal in the prenatal period. Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 300% increase of CD71high Ter119low proerythroblasts (R2) but a 20-fold reduction of reticulocytes and erythrocytes (R5). Erythroid cell maturation in Lsd1-deficient embryos is impaired at the transition from proerythroblasts/R2 to basophilic erythroblasts/R3. Enucleated mature definitive erythroid cells were markedly reduced, and embryos were small with pale fetal livers at E13.5. These data demonstrate that Lsd1 is essential for terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C57-C63 are supported by flow cytometry data (C58, C59) shown in Figure 4D,E, blood smear data (C61), and embryo images (C62). The conclusion (C63) is appropriately inferred from the combined data showing differentiation defects in both granulocytic and erythroid lineages.

result: Several genes typically highly expressed in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (e.g., CD34, HoxA9, Sca-1) were substantially upregulated in Lsd1 mutant cells. The stem/progenitor cell gene signature was highly enriched across all assayed Lsd1-deficient cells (Gr1dim Mac1+ cells, CD71+c-Kit+ proerythroblasts, CD150+ CD48- LS+K+ HSCs) with highly significant NES scores and FDR values. Hox genes and HoxA9 target genes were significantly upregulated. The authors hypothesize that failure to repress earlier lineage gene expression programs impairs early and later hematopoietic maturation programs.
evaluation: Claims C64-C69 are supported by gene expression profiling data (C64), GSEA analysis (C65, C67, C69), qPCR data (C66), and pathway analysis (C68) shown in Figure 5 and supplementary figures. The hypothesis (C70) is appropriately labeled as speculation and is based on the gene expression data. The statistical significance is strong with appropriate FDR corrections.

result: A total of 25,173 Lsd1 binding sites (peaks) were identified from ChIP-Seq data in 32D cells. 16 out of 18 (>85%) Lsd1 binding sites identified in 32D cells were validated by ChIP-qPCR in primary Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. Lsd1 binding peaks were predominantly positioned at intergenic (40%) and intronic (38%) regions with limited binding to proximal promoters (15%). Lsd1 occupied 55% of genes (1361 out of 2473) that were at least 1.5-fold upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells.
evaluation: Claims C71-C74 are supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis (C71, C73, C74) and ChIP-qPCR validation (C72) shown in Figure 5G-H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A. The validation rate of >85% (C72) provides confidence in the ChIP-Seq data quality. The use of a cell line (32D) for ChIP-Seq is a limitation, but validation in primary cells strengthens the findings.

result: No differences in global H3K4me1/me2 and H3K9me1/me2 methylation levels were detected between wild-type and Lsd1 knockout cells by Western blot. Lsd1 occupied about three times more putative enhancers than active promoters. Both KO-specific promoter and enhancer peak target genes correlated highly with genes upregulated in Lsd1 knockout Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. These findings indicate that Lsd1 represses gene expression in association with changes in H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 levels at enhancers and promoters, respectively.
evaluation: Claims C75-C78 are supported by Western blot data (C75), ChIP-Seq overlap analysis (C76), and integrative analysis (C77) shown in Figure 6A-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B. The conclusion (C78) is appropriately inferred from the correlation between KO-specific histone marks and gene upregulation. The lack of global changes (C75) is important as it indicates Lsd1 acts locally at specific genomic regions.

result: KO-specific enhancer-associated H3K4me1 and promoter-associated H3K4me2 peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes with highly significant enrichment scores and p-values. KO-specific peak target genes were not meaningfully enriched in the granulocyte gene signature. Genes with Lsd1 bound at distal sites and promoter were highly enriched in the LSK signature, while genes with Lsd1 bound only at distal regions were slightly but significantly enriched. None of the three Lsd1 binding groups were significantly enriched in the granulocyte signature. These data suggest that Lsd1 is directly involved in the repression of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell genes but not in the activation of mature granulocyte genes. Lsd1 occupies distal regulatory regions as well as proximal promoters of stem and progenitor cell genes, and deletion of Lsd1 is associated with increased levels of H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 on enhancers and promoters of HSPC genes.
evaluation: Claims C79-C88 are supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6E-G and ChIP-Seq data analysis. The statistical significance is strong with appropriate p-values. The conclusion (C85) is appropriately inferred from the selective enrichment in LSK but not granulocyte signatures. The identification of specific genes (C86) provides biological validation of the findings.

result: Conditional deletion of Lsd1 resulted in severe pancytopenia, the consequence of combined defects in early hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and terminal blood cell maturation. Lsd1 is an indispensable factor for hematopoietic differentiation, crucial for immature hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and critical for differentiation of mature hematopoietic cells. Lsd1-deficient HSCs were severely impaired in their capacity to mature into immature progenitors. Deletion of Lsd1 strongly interfered with terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation. Differentiating Lsd1 knockout cells aberrantly express HSPC genes normally expressed only in HSCs and progenitors. The authors propose that failure to silence LSK-associated genes in Lsd1 mutants interferes with proper differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C89-C96 represent the main conclusions of the study, integrating findings from all experimental approaches. These conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive data from conditional knockout mice, transplantation experiments, colony assays, flow cytometry, gene expression profiling, and ChIP-Seq analysis. The proposed model (C96) is appropriately labeled as speculation and is based on all experimental findings.

result: Background knowledge claims about Lsd1 biochemical function, histone methylation marks, and chromatin biology. These include Lsd1's demethylase activity on H3K4/K9, the distribution of H3K4 methylation marks at promoters and enhancers, the enzymes that catalyze H3K4 methylation and demethylation, and Lsd1's function in repressor complexes.
evaluation: Claims C1, C10-C19 are established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies. These claims provide necessary background context for the study but are not novel findings. The citations appear appropriate and the knowledge claims are consistent with the field.

result: Prior work on Lsd1 deletion showing embryonic lethality, developmental arrest around E5.5-E7.5, proliferation and differentiation defects in ESCs, and potential vulnerability of acute myeloid leukemia cells to Lsd1 inhibition.
evaluation: Claims C20-C23 are based on previous studies cited in the manuscript. These claims provide important context for the current study by establishing what was known about Lsd1 function prior to this work. The citations appear appropriate.

result: Discussion of Lsd1 as a potential drug target in hematopoietic malignancies and β-hemoglobinopathies, with cautionary notes about potential side effects based on the severe hematopoietic defects observed upon Lsd1 deletion.
evaluation: Claims C97-C98 are based on previous studies cited. Claims C99 and C110 are appropriately cautious statements inferred from the severe hematopoietic defects observed in this study. The authors appropriately note that appreciable or complete inhibition of Lsd1 could have undesired side effects, which is a reasonable inference from their data.

result: Comparison of Lsd1 function in ES cells versus mature myeloid cells, showing that Lsd1 occupies only about 30% of active enhancers in mature myeloid cells compared to virtually all enhancers in ES cells. Discussion of differences in chromatin architecture between ES cells, fetal cells, and adult cells, suggesting a differential requirement for Lsd1 in ES cells versus mature cells.
evaluation: Claims C100-C104 are supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis (C100) and established knowledge from previous studies (C101-C103). The inference of differential requirement for Lsd1 (C104) is appropriately drawn from comparing the current data with previous ES cell studies. This represents an important insight about context-dependent Lsd1 function.

result: Discussion of potential indirect effects of Lsd1 deletion, including destabilization of the CoREST complex leading to increased H3K56 acetylation, and effects on Dnmt1 stability. The authors note that Dnmt1 knockout animals show subtle hematopoietic phenotypes, making it unlikely that Dnmt1 destabilization accounts for the severe phenotypes observed.
evaluation: Claims C105-C108 are based on previous studies cited. The authors appropriately discuss potential indirect effects of Lsd1 deletion and provide reasoning for why Dnmt1 destabilization is unlikely to account for the observed phenotypes. This represents appropriate consideration of alternative explanations.

result: Main conclusions of the study: Lsd1 is an indispensible epigenetic governor of hematopoietic differentiation that represses HSPC gene expression programs during hematopoietic differentiation. Lsd1 acts at transcription start sites as well as enhancer regions. Loss of Lsd1 is associated with increased H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 methylation on HSPC genes and gene derepression. Failure to fully silence HSPC genes compromises differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells and mature blood cell lineages. Lsd1-mediated concurrent repression of enhancer and promoter activity of stem and progenitor cell genes is a pivotal epigenetic mechanism required for proper hematopoietic maturation. The authors propose that Lsd1 is an epigenetic governor required broadly for repression of stem cell gene expression programs during embryonic stem cell as well as somatic cell differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C2-C9 and C109 represent the main conclusions of the study, integrating findings from all experimental approaches. These conclusions are well-supported by comprehensive data from conditional knockout mice, transplantation experiments, colony assays, flow cytometry, gene expression profiling, and ChIP-Seq analysis. The proposal that Lsd1 is required broadly for stem cell gene repression (C109) is appropriately labeled as speculation and represents an extrapolation from the hematopoietic data.
